column1: # Paper-style design, following Narasimhan et al. 2019 (Science 365, eaat7487), Supplement S4.3 "Proximal modeling".
# Use:  DESIGN=narasimhan sbatch --export=ALL run_qpwave_qpadm.sh        (see README, section "Narasimhan-style design")
# How the paper models a population from the Copper Age onward:
#   * RIGHT = a small FIXED set of pre-Copper-Age populations (RightAll, 8 populations). Candidate sources are NEVER rotated onto the right.
#         RightAll = Ethiopia_4500BP, EEHG, WSHG, PPN, WEHG, Anatolia_N, Ganj_Dareh_N, ESHG
#   * LEFT  = proximal sources close in space and time (their Table S7), up to 3 sources.
#   * accept a model at p > 0.01 and only if every weight's 95% CI (+-2 SE) lies inside [0,1];
#   * then "model competition": sources of a competing model are added to the right and the model is re-tested.
# Substitutions forced by this dataset: Ethiopia_4500BP -> modern Mbuti; ESHG (Lake Baikal, not in the dataset) -> Chukchi (n=1);
#   PPN -> Levant pre-pottery Neolithic from Jordan (JOR_PPNB, 2 samples, + JOR_PPNC, 1 sample; the 'rel' in the JOR_PPNC label refers to I1699,
#     which is not in this dataset, so there is no relative pair in the data and the sample is kept);
#   WSHG is a single genome here (3 in the paper).
# role = pool | right_base | ignore   (same meaning as in pop_pools.tsv)
# ---------------- LEFT: proximal candidate sources (paper's Table S7 where available) ----------------
# Iran / Turan (Table S7: Hajji_Firuz_C, Tepe_Hissar_C, Shahr_I_Sokhta_BA1, Parkhai_Anau_EN, Sarazm_EN, Geoksyur_EN, BMAC)
# Iron Age Iranian groups are not in the paper's source list; they stay out (as in the default design)
# South Asia (Table S7: Indus_Periphery_Pool and SPGT are both proximal sources; here 1 + 1 individual)
# East Asia: modern Han as the proxy (the paper also uses present-day proxies where ancient DNA is missing)
